His sole success in his native Germany came on the Flat, over just short of two miles, while he also scored over an extended 10 furlongs at Dundalk after. Shock Listowel maiden hurdle winner Kingdom Calling showed a bit more when third at Limerick last time and he can go close. Silas Marner is another to consider.

Those early efforts were understandably a bit below what she's achieved since on turf but were likely a consequence of improvement rather than an aversion to synthetic surfaces. George Scott's mare won't have to find much extra, if any, off just a 2lb rise and holds solid claims. Way Of Life and Westridge also arrive in relatively good nick and should give the selection most to do. Westridge is marginally preferred having made a very encouraging start to this campaign when 5th of 14 in a class 4 handicap at Newbury. This trip suited well then and there's surely more to come on only his 7th start. Way Of Life was winless last year but knocked on the door regularly and he should once again be in the mix but may lack a gear over this sharper trip than ideal

selections.comment: Of those with experience it's a very tight call between RENEWAL, who improved markedly on second start last term when upped to this seven furlongs and Sea Poetry, winner of his sole start in November (over 7f). The former just gets the nod given the value of his second to Celestial Orbit was inflated by that one going on to land a Listed event next time. The form of Sea Poetry's win has also been franked with a host of future winners behind him that day but not at quite such elevated heights. The biggest challenge to the principals above may come from a newcomer and heading that list is the Gosden's Chilli Salt, a Too Darn Hot filly who is a full sister to Jazz Scene, a winner at a mile, and a half-sister to the high class miler Random Harvest

selections.comment: This can go to KOSOMETSUKE who looks to have been treated leniently by the assessor for his first handicap assignment and can open his account to kick off a fruitful campaign. Roger Varian's gelding showed promise in all three runs last term over an inadequate looking 6f in some decent novice races. The step up to 7f should suit well and off a mark of 65 getting weight from all the field could prove well up to the task. Penelope Valentine is interesting back over the same course and distance of her sole victory in February and is feared most. Noble Guest could go well and fill the frame. George Margarson's gelding was a bit disappointing the last twice back on turf but did well off a layoff over course and distance prior off a mark of 73 when beaten under 4l. He's been given a chance by the assessor now down to 67 and stripping fitter and is entitled to go close

selections.comment: A chance is taken with DASH OF AZURE in a very trappy affair. Ralph Beckett's filly ran three solid races in defeat last term finding one too good on each occasion, including over course and distance when last seen in October. Fitness is taken on trust (ran to a similar level on career debut as two other runs) and from a potentially lenient opening mark she should go very well. Drawn on the innner she can get an early handy pitch and kick on in the straight. Al Khawassaa is a big threat but needs to bounce back from a dismal run last time when kicking off this year's campaign. However, she endured a miserable trip all round at Beverley and can be shown in a much better light today. She can go close. Bridget's View, another on a workable looking mark for handicap debut and a course and distance winner to boot can just edge it over Primrose Path and Rockymountainway for minor honours despite the slightly off-putting widest berth (she has the running style to get an early position at least even if having to use a bit too much fuel early)

selections.comment: Hat-trick seeking ATA RANGI can take this. Ed Walker's gelding made a taking stable/Uk debut last time wining a class 4 handicap over course and distance showing a tidy turn of foot. There looks to be a fair bit more in the locker and with a decent draw in stall two for a prominent racer everything looks in place for another top effort. He'll be difficult to topple. Artic Dawn is probably best placed to do so having run right up to his best on season debut at Southwell last time. With this being only his seventh start he can be expected to build on that fine return effort. He should see out the mile and poses a big threat to all. Glam Squad, another to show a bit more last time, can just edge out Superposition to make the frame

selections.comment: All the field have questions to answer and it could be worthing chancing CURRUMBIN can get back on track following a lack-lustre effort returned to the turf last time at Goodwood. Before that he won a 2m event at Chelmsford in February and followed that up with a length second over course and distance on penultimate start. He's much more reliable on the AW and given misgivings about the rest of the field would have a good chance of landing this without having to find extra despite the 2lb rise since the defeat to Further Measure (on a hat-trick that day and winner again next time out) over course and distance. Capone would be a big danger if wound up for this season opener. On balance he looks likely to need this but may still reach the frame. The admirably consistent Doublethetrouble is next best. He hasn't been beaten more than 3.5l in his last nine runs and is now just 4lb above his last winning mark. He shouldn't be far away again

Gonnino is another who was given a considerate ride last time and can run into a place if getting a stiff test down in trip.

selections.comment: An open race where it could pay to take a chance on previous C&D winner SAINT ARVANS. He is on a long losing run but the handicapper has relented and he should come on massively for his latest outing where the ground was too soft. His biggest danger looks to be class dropper Whistleinthedark who looked a huge threat until a race ending error late on last time. He is another who has tumbled down the weights having run well in the Scottish National just last year. If his jumping holds up he should be thereabouts. Veteran Everyday Champagne isn't dismissed either in and open race given his good course form last summer. He is forgiven his latest run where he needed the outing.

selections.comment: A well up-to-scratch renewal. The Lion In Winter will do for many, as the unbeaten form pick, representing an all-conquering yard which has dominated the trials thus far and with a pedigree suggesting this trip will suit the Derby favourite as a 3yo now. He may well win but is a very short price considering he's been off for nine months with minor setbacks (last season) and then being a bit behind fitness-wise in early spring, while the last of his trainer's four wins in this came back in 2010. At much bigger prices, a chance is taken on DAMYSUS, who gave the strong impression that he would improve for the experience when notably green en route to a highly promising return at Sandown last month. This demands more for sure but this colt will know more now and may just be up it. Unbeaten Alpine Trail has been supplemented and can go very well. He may be next best ahead of The Lion In Winter.

selections.comment: Rusesellsbelle has looked unlucky on her last couple of outings coming down when looking a huge threat. She is entitled to come on for that last run and looks a huge threat but will need to improve again to beat BELLE THE TIGRESS. The selection did disappoint when last seen at the start of the year but that came on unsuitably soft ground and her previous placed effort reads very well. She split future winners that day and the pair ahead of her have both run with credit at Graded level since. If back to that level of form she will be tough to beat. Rhythm Of Life shaped well last time and the runner up has boosted the form in a strong handicap so she can grab a place here.

selections.comment: EXPOUND is unexposed in this sphere and is open to plenty of improvement having already won in this discipline and multiple times on the flat. He went too fast on his last hurdles run but was a flat winner off 76 last time so has plenty of mileage in his current mark. Another dual purpose performer Fascinating Shadow may prove the biggest threat. He hinted at a revival on the level last time and is entitled to come on for that outing. He managed to place off 2lb higher in this discipline last summer and with the good ground in his favour should run well for an in form stable. Miss Gherkin has shown a consistent level of form in this sphere other than when tiring on soft ground last time and can complete the places here.

Mustang Mozzie was highly tried last year and though he was ultimately well held last time the winner did go on to success at Graded level at Aintree. He is feared most dropping in grade back from a break ahead of the experienced Dancing Dame. She has had plenty of chances but brings in a decent level of form so should run well if fit after a break
